title: The Sapporo Miso
description: You're warm, a little indulgent, and you show up for people when it's cold outside. You'd rather over-deliver on comfort than hold back.
whyItFits: Sapporo Miso's rich, fermented depth and generous, warming character matches your instinct to go all-in on comfort.

title: The Hakata Tonkotsu
description: You believe the famous spot is famous for a reason, and you're patient enough to prove it. Once you commit to something, you commit all the way.
whyItFits: Hakata Tonkotsu's hours-long emulsified broth rewards exactly that kind of patience and full commitment.

title: The Tokyo Shoyu
description: You're the reliable one -- balanced, unfussy, and quietly excellent rather than loud about it. People trust your taste precisely because it isn't showing off.
whyItFits: Tokyo Shoyu is ramen's own reference point -- balanced and restrained, not because it lacks ambition, but because restraint is the whole skill.

title: The Hakodate Shio
description: You're understated and precise. You'd rather do less, better, than pile on more just to be noticed.
whyItFits: Hakodate Shio is built entirely around restraint and clarity -- proof that a lighter touch can still be the most memorable one in the room.

title: The Kitakata
description: You're resourceful and low-key -- you don't need a big production to enjoy something fully, and you're just as happy with a simple, honest routine.
whyItFits: Kitakata's whole identity is unpretentious -- a light, dependable bowl locals eat for breakfast without a second thought.

title: The Yokohama Iekei
description: You're bold and unapologetic about what you want -- rich flavor, no compromises, and you're not afraid to ask for exactly how you like it.
whyItFits: Iekei shops are famous for taking detailed customer requests -- richness, noodle firmness, extra fat -- which suits someone who knows exactly what they want.

title: The Asahikawa
description: You care about the story behind things, and you'll go out of your way to find something with real history rather than settling for whatever's closest.
whyItFits: Asahikawa's double-soup method and insulating oil layer are a direct, functional response to its climate and history -- a bowl built by necessity, not trend.

title: The Kumamoto
description: You're bold, social, and a little intense in the best way -- you'd rather make an experience out of something than eat it and move on.
whyItFits: Kumamoto's signature black garlic oil is assertive and memorable -- a bowl that announces itself, the same way you do.
